title: LIV Golf Accuses DP World Tour of Interference as Bankruptcy Judge Clears Contract Purge
excerpt: In a New Jersey Chapter 11 hearing, LIV's lawyer called Europe's no-dual-membership rule a "clear attempt to interfere" — while the court let LIV tear up 19 player contracts, DeChambeau's and Johnson's among them.
body:
• LIV Golf's lawyer told a New Jersey bankruptcy hearing on Wednesday that the DP World Tour's new hard line — no membership for anyone playing LIV next season — is a "clear attempt to interfere" with LIV's restructuring.
  • The court approved LIV's motion to reject the current contracts of 19 golfers, including Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson, as the league rebuilds as "LIV 2.0."
  • LIV says it will know by the end of October whether it can continue in its new form; its future has been in doubt since Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew support and the league filed for Chapter 11.
  • The DP World Tour's stance ends the conditional releases that let players such as Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton compete on both circuits — and protected their Ryder Cup eligibility.

LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of a "clear attempt to interfere" with its restructuring, after the European circuit said it would refuse membership to anyone who plays on the breakaway league next season. The charge was made during a bankruptcy court hearing on Wednesday, where LIV's future — in a slimmed-down form its lawyers call LIV 2.0 — is being decided, according to BBC Sport's account of the proceedings.

What Was Said in Court

Rob Fitzgerald of Gibson Dunn, representing LIV, told the hearing the organisation was "quite concerned" by the DP World Tour's position. The timing, he argued, struck at LIV's negotiations with its own players and its reorganisation at large, and raised the same anti-competitive concerns LIV has pressed before about rival leagues boxing out its players. LIV reserved all rights and remedies over the statements.

"Player freedom is the reason LIV Golf was created, and it's the foundation of LIV Golf 2.0, a league built around its players."

— Rob Fitzgerald, Gibson Dunn, attorney for LIV Golf

The DP World Tour declined to comment on Fitzgerald's statement, but its chief executive, Guy Kinnings, had told BBC Sport on Monday that "players need to make a choice," toughening a policy under which some stars previously received conditional releases to play both tours. Judge Kaplan acknowledged he had heard Kinnings' comments and that they raised concerns.

Contracts Torn Up, Clock Ticking

The same hearing approved LIV's motion to reject the current contracts of 19 golfers, which the league said do not reflect the compensation structure contemplated under LIV 2.0. The list includes Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson, who had sought clarity on whether rejection would free them to talk to third parties about their playing futures. Fitzgerald said LIV would know by the end of the month whether it can continue as LIV 2.0 — a timeline GOLF.com described as the league identifying viable paths through restructuring or an orderly wind-down.

How Golf Got Here

LIV launched in 2022 with Saudi financing and guaranteed contracts that split men's golf. Its players were banned from the PGA Tour but kept a foothold in Europe: DP World Tour membership, maintained through conditional releases and payment of fines, was also the route to European Ryder Cup eligibility. Earlier this year, nine LIV players were granted conditional releases for the 2026 season. That bridge is now being withdrawn for 2027. The league's position weakened sharply this autumn when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial support and LIV filed for Chapter 11 protection in New Jersey.

Why Players Are Caught in the Middle

For golfers under contract, the two announcements collide: LIV is tearing up existing deals to renegotiate cheaper ones, while Europe is telling them that signing a new LIV deal ends their DP World Tour membership — and with it, a realistic path to the 2027 Ryder Cup in Ireland. Front Office Sports noted that the PGA Tour is not currently planning a special programme for returning LIV players either, which narrows the exits further. The end-of-October restructuring verdict will decide whether LIV 2.0 is a league players can still choose, or a closing door.
